scenes.heading: Chromatography
scenes.sub: Separating a mixture to see what's inside
scenes.say: Is this medicine pure? Is there a banned drug in an athlete's urine? How much caffeine is in an energy drink? Chromatography separates mixtures so you can find out.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Friends who stop at every shop fall behind the crowd
scenes.science: Components stuck to the stationary phase move slowly
scenes.breaks: friends choose shops, but molecules are held back by intermolecular forces, like hydrogen bonds to silica.
scenes.say: Picture friends walking through a shopping centre with the crowd. The shops are the stationary phase, and the moving crowd is the mobile phase. A friend who keeps stopping at shops falls behind. One who goes with the flow reaches the exit first.

scenes.heading: How the separation works
points: Very soluble in mobile phase: moves fast
Like holds like: polar holds polar
scenes.say: Each component keeps sticking to the stationary phase and dissolving back into the mobile phase. Strongly adsorbed components move slowly; very soluble ones move fast. It's about intermolecular forces: a polar stationary phase, like paper or silica, holds back polar components.

scenes.heading: The Rf value
scenes.say: In paper or thin-layer chromatography, each spot gets an R f value: the distance the spot moved divided by the distance the solvent front moved, both from the origin line. It's always between zero and one. Same conditions, same R f.
scenes.caption: In paper or thin-layer chromatography, each spot gets an Rf value: the distance the spot moved ÷ the distance the solvent front moved, both from the origin line. It's always between 0 and 1. Same conditions, same Rf.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: The solvent front moves 8.0 cm. A dye gives spots at 2.4 cm and 6.0 cm. References: X 0.30, Y 0.55, Z 0.75.
lines: The food dye is a mixture of X and Z
scenes.say: Two point four over eight point zero is zero point three zero, matching dye X. Six point zero over eight point zero is zero point seven five, matching dye Z. So the food dye is a mixture of X and Z.
scenes.caption: 2.4 ÷ 8.0 is 0.30, matching dye X. 6.0 ÷ 8.0 is 0.75, matching dye Z. So the food dye is a mixture of X and Z.

scenes.heading: TLC vs HPLC

right.title: HPLC
points: Liquid pumped through a packed column
Peak area is proportional to amount

scenes.say: Thin-layer chromatography tells you what's there. High-performance liquid chromatography, or HPLC, also tells you how much. A liquid is pumped at high pressure through a packed column. Retention time identifies each substance, and peak area is proportional to the amount.

scenes.heading: Using a calibration curve
scenes.say: To find a concentration, run standard solutions and plot peak area against concentration. Run the unknown under the same conditions, read its concentration off the line, and multiply by any dilution factor. Keep it inside the range of your standards.

Quick recap. Stationary sticks, mobile moves. R f is the spot distance over the solvent front. In HPLC, retention time tells you what, and peak area tells you how much. Now try the practice questions!
